items_missed: Set the Agenda: no 'how are you today,' no agenda statement (what we'll cover / how long it takes), never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
Probe: didn't ask about storage stops, additional stops, or narrow hallways/tight turns at either address.
Quote/Booking: never mentioned that no deposit is required, didn't ask 'any other questions before I let you go,' didn't state branch hours or how to reach the office.

Politeness: never used the customer's actual name once in the call (relied on 'sir' throughout) — also got his name backwards while taking it down, logging first name as 'Rad' and last as 'Memori' instead of Mamori Morad.

Bonus: didn't acknowledge or build on the customer's opening joke about being 'sick of AI talking to AI,' gave no No Worries Damage Coverage or 60c/lb insurance explanation, only explained the travel fee after the customer pushed back on it rather than getting ahead of it, and didn't use any budget-conscious framing despite the customer signaling he was comparison shopping against a competitor.
top_strength: Therese moved efficiently through move details -- both addresses, square footage, bedroom count, packing needs, and a box-count gut-check -- and correctly caught that the destination home's size meant this needed a virtual walkthrough instead of a phone quote, then locked the walkthrough in for that same evening at 5pm so the lead didn't go cold.
coaching_note: Use his name -- you never said 'Mamori' or even a corrected version once in 12 minutes, it was 'sir' the whole way through, and you actually wrote his name down backwards. When he said 'so you guys gonna charge me to come to my house basically,' that's a customer bristling at a fee -- meet it with reassurance and context, not just 'that is correct, sir.' Also don't skip the agenda opener or the 'any other questions before I let you go' close -- he's about to hop on a video call with a stranger tonight, and those small trust-builders matter before you hand him off.
phone_presence_notes: Courteous but scripted throughout -- repeated 'gotcha'/'alright' fillers, no name use, and no acknowledgment of the customer's opening joke or his pushback on the travel fee.
audio_review_reason: Phone presence scored 2 (Flat) -- verify actual vocal tone/warmth on the recording rather than relying on transcript text alone.
